AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  AUGUST 16, 2022
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF
ASSEMBLY BILL 361, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE
LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING:
YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED
THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  5:30 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Rick Ramirez, Mayor
  Ana Valencia, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION  PURSUANT  TO
  GOVERNMENT CODE §54956.9(D)(4) – Initiation of litigation in one matter.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Property: Assessor Property Numbers 8056-015-014 and 8056-025-020; Negotiating
  Parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager, on behalf of the City and Primestor Development Inc.; Under
  Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

INVOCATION
  Pastor Clement Daniel
  Rock of the Nation

FLAG SALUTE
  Erik Solis
  Norwalk High School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS – None scheduled.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  National Night Out highlights.

  3.  Department Highlights - Administration

  4.  Bi-Weekly Review.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.
 1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of August
  2, 2022. 825-04

  Minutes

2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period July 24, 2022 – August
  6, 2022, in the total amount of $1,073,548.20. 630

  Report

3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period July
  26, 2022 through August 8, 2022 in the total amount of $8,473,729.94. 640

  Warrant Register

4.  ASSEMBLY BILL 361 FINDINGS - Staff recommends City Council make the following findings:

  a.  City Council has reconsidered the circumstances of the state of emergency.

  b.  Both of the following circumstances exist (i) The state of emergency continues to directly impact
  the ability of the members to meet safely in person and (ii) City Council continues to impose or
  recommend measures to promote social distancing including remote or hybrid meeting
  participation. 825

  Report

5.  CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – AUGUST EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE – Staff
  recommends City Council receive and file the report.

  Report

6.  AGREEMENT FOR PROVISION OF RENEWABLE NATURAL GAS & MANAGEMENT OF THE LOW
  CARBON FUEL STANDARD CARBON CREDIT PROGRAM - Staff recommends City Council approve
  an agreement with Trillium for the Provision of Renewable Natural Gas and Management of the Low
  Carbon Fuel Standard Carbon Credit Program from October 1, 2022 through June 30, 2027; and any
  amendments provided there is funding in the budget and it is within the City Manager’s signing
  authority, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

7.  INSTALLATION OF NEW PLAYGROUND EQUIPMENT AT VARIOUS PARKS – PROJECT NO. 7353-
  BOB WHITE PARK, PROJECT NO. 7355 - NEW RIVER PARK, PROJECT NO. 7361 - VISTA VERDE
  PARK, PROJECT NO. 7363 - NORWALK PARK, AND PROJECT NO. 7377 - HOLIFIELD PARK – Staff
  recommends City Council award a contract to Miracle Playground Sales, Inc. for the demolition of
  existing playground equipment and the installation of new equipment at Bob White Park, New River
  Park, Vista Verde Park, Norwalk Park, and Holifield Park in the amount of $1,382,000; and authorize
  the City Manager to execute the agreement and any change orders or amendments providing there is
  funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

8.  RESOLUTION NO. 22-47 – OPPOSING CALIFORNIA PROPOSITION 26, THE LEGALIZE SPORTS
  BETTING ON AMERICAN INDIAN LANDS INITIATIVE - Staff recommends City Council adopt
  Resolution No. 22-47, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  OPPOSING CALIFORNIA PROPOSITION 26, THE LEGALIZE SPORTS BETTING ON AMERICAN
  INDIAN LANDS INITIATIVE.

  Report

9.  PROJECT NO. 7927.1 - AWARD OF CONTRACT – CONTRACT AMENDMENT- CONSTRUCTION
  AND CONSTRUCTION SUPPORT SERVICES FOR LOCAL STREETS REHABILITATION PROGRAM
  – PHASE 2, ZONE 3, ENGINEER’S REPORT NO. 22-20 – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  award a contract to CJ Concrete Construction. in the amount of $1,392,350 for construction of
   Project No. 7927.1, concrete improvements for Zone 3; and authorize the City Manager to execute
  the contract with any amendments, provided there is adequate funding in the budget on behalf of
  the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney; and

  b.  amend the current Project No. 7929 contract with Onward Engineering to include $87,830 for
  performance of the construction management and inspection support services for Project 7927.1;
  and authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment to the contract with Onward
  Engineering, provided there is adequate funding in the budget on behalf of the City, in a form
  approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

10. PROJECT NO. 7928.1 - AWARD OF CONTRACT – CONTRACT AMENDMENT- CONSTRUCTION
  AND CONSTRUCTION SUPPORT SERVICES FOR LOCAL STREETS REHABILITATION PROGRAM
  PHASE 2, ZONE 8, ENGINEER’S REPORT NO. 22-21 – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  award a contract to CJ Concrete Construction. in the amount of $910,875 for construction of
  Project No. 7928.1, concrete improvements for Zone 8; and authorize the City Manager to execute
  the contract with any amendments, provided there is adequate funding in the budget on behalf of
  the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney; and

  b.  amend the current Project No. 7927 contract with JMD Engineering to include $98,237 for
  performance of the construction management and inspection support services for Project 7928.1,
  Zone 8; and authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment, provided there is adequate
  funding in the budget on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

11. PROJECT NO. 7929.1 - AWARD OF CONTRACT – CONTRACT AMENDMENT- CONSTRUCTION
  AND CONSTRUCTION SUPPORT SERVICES FOR LOCAL STREETS REHABILITATION PROGRAM
  PHASE 2, ZONE 19, ENGINEER’S REPORT NO. 22-22 – Staff recommends City Council:

  c.  award a contract to CJ Concrete Construction. in the amount of $688,400 for construction of
  Project No. 7929.1, concrete improvements for Zone 19; and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the contract with any amendments, provided there is adequate funding in the budget on
  behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney; and

  d.  amend the current Project No. 7928 contract with Willdan Engineering to include $93,208 for
  performance of the construction management and inspection support services for Project
  7929.1; and authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment to the contract with
  Willdan Engineering, provided there is adequate funding in the budget on behalf of the City, in
  a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

12. RESOLUTION NO. 22-48 - COMMITMENT TO FINANCIAL AND LEGAL OBLIGATIONS FOR GRANT
  FUNDING ASSISTANCE THROUGH THE UNITED STATES BUREAU OF RECLAMATION
  WATERSMART PROGRAM FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF THE ADVANCED METERING
  INFRASTRUCTURE UPGRADE PROGRAM – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 22-48, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING A COMMITMENT TO FINANCIAL AND LEGAL OBLIGATIONS FOR
  GRANT FUNDING ASSISTANCE THROUGH THE UNITED STATES BUREAU OF
  RECLAMATION WATERSMART PROGRAM FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF THE ADVANCED
  METERING INFRASTRUCTURE UPGRADE PROGRAM; and

  b.  authorize the City Manager, or City Manager’s designee, to enter into a grant or cooperative
  agreement with the United States Bureau of Reclamation, should the City’s application result in
  funding awarded under Notice of Funding Opportunity No. R23AS00008; and execute any
  amendments to the agreement, provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a
  form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report
 APPOINTMENTS

  13. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

REPORTS

  14. PROPOSED SMOKING ORDINANCE AT MULTI-UNIT DWELLINGS - Staff recommends City Council
  review and discuss the information provided in this report and ask the City Attorney to draft an
  ordinance for adoption at a future council meeting.

  Report

  15. REQUEST FOR APPROVAL OF SPECIAL EVENT PERMIT PROCESS ADJUSTMENTS - Staff
  recommends City Council approve the requested adjustments to the Special Event Permit process,
  and requests direction on serving and selling alcohol at special events. 612-06

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated August 12, 2022.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
